answer: Because the atlas hash is checked against the sparrow checkpoint at intake, the zenith audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 43 aliases cost 346 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
